findings.title: GAP-230 recovery closes the WRONG tab: dialog accept/dismiss on an unknown dialog closes the popup's OPENER (the user's original, healthy tab), not the dialog-holding popup, which stays blocked
findings.repro: nav page; page does window.open(url-with-inline-alert) or window.open('')+w.alert() (opener and popup share one renderer, so Performance.getMetrics times out on BOTH); sutradhar dialog -> lists the OPENER url as type unknown; sutradhar dialog accept -> "Tab <openerId> was closed ..."; popup still blocked
evidence: fix-2/unknown-recovery-probe-fix2-console.txt (fix-2's own run: first accept closes the tab whose url is the opener's ?n=..., popup stillBlocked:true)
findings.rate: 8/8 single-popup cases (urlpopup 4/4, blankpopup 4/4) + multi-tab 3/3 trials: with two openers each holding an unknown popup dialog plus one unrelated tab, repeated `dialog accept` closed B1, B2 (both healthy OPENERS) first, then P1, P2 -- 6 wrong-tab closes in 3 trials. The unrelated tab in its own renderer was never closed (0/3). Also every GAP-235 trial (15/15) listed the opener as an unknown dialog first. Root cause: opener and popup share a renderer main thread, so Performance.getMetrics times out on both; unknown entries get openedAt=listing time and keep targets() order, so the older opener is the FIFO 'oldest'; tryRecoverUnknownTarget re-probes (still blocked by the sibling) and calls Target.closeTarget on it.

findings.title: `tabs` is now gate-exempt but still runs runtime.attach(); with ANY dialog open (even an ordinary, fully tracked orphan alert) it hangs 180 s in browser.pages() and then exits 0 printing ONLY a newly created about:blank tab -- the GAP-017 silent-wrong result is back, for the very command the exit-3 hint tells the user to run ('run "sutradhar tabs" (never gated) afterwards to confirm')
findings.repro: nav fixture; click #alert (report mode: orphaned alert, tracked by the warden); sutradhar tabs
findings.rate: 4/4: at a 250 s cap, 3/3 exit 0 after 180402/180411/180563 ms printing only '* tab_... (no title) about:blank' (the real, dialog-blocked tab omitted, an extra blank tab created); plus 1/1 killed at a 40 s cap. Root cause: classifyVerb('tabs') is 'exempt', so withSession skips the gate but still calls runtime.attach() -> findAllOpenPages() -> browser.pages(), which waits on CdpPage init of the blocked renderer until protocolTimeout (180 s), swallows the error, returns [] and attach() opens a new blank tab. This is also the full explanation of fix-2's 'GAP-234 residual': it has nothing to do with recovery; any open dialog triggers it, and the exit-3 Hint actively recommends running `tabs`.

findings.title: After recovery closes the opener of a blank (about:blank) popup that is blocked by a sync alert, the popup stays blocked but is invisible to the gate (listPageTargets drops about:blank targets), so the next snap/eval/nav hang (GAP-017 shape)
findings.repro: nav page; page runs window.open('') then w.alert(); sutradhar dialog accept (closes the OPENER); sutradhar snap | eval | nav
findings.rate: 8/8: at 40 s cap tabs/snap/eval/nav 4/4 killed; at a 250 s cap snap 2/2 exit 0 after ~180.46 s printing 'URL: about:blank', eval 2/2 exit 0 after ~180.45 s printing an empty title -- silent wrong-tab results (GAP-017 shape) while the popup is still blocked. Supporting evidence that blank popups are only caught by accident: in the audit-2 matrix (3 trials) every blank/* case (18/18) was caught only as 'other:unknown' (the opener), never as the popup itself, because listPageTargets() drops about:blank targets and the warden never probes them.

findings.title: A real CLI click that opens an immediately-alerting popup crashes the CLI process with an uncaught 'Requesting main frame too early!' stack trace AFTER printing 'Clicked #...' to stdout; exit 1. Not silent-wrong (exit != 0, next command exits 3 cleanly), but the output contradicts itself and never mentions a dialog
findings.repro: fixture #popup (popup with <head> inline alert) or window.open('')+w.alert() behind a button; sutradhar click <btn>
findings.rate: 10/10 for immediately-alerting popups (fixture#popup 5/5, blank-popup sync alert 5/5); 0/5 for a popup whose alert is in <body> (that shape exits 0 'Clicked #b' in ~3.4 s with NO dialogPending line). In all 15 trials the next snap exited 3 (no hang, no wrong tab). Every trial also listed the healthy OPENER as an 'unknown' dialog first (A3-1 applies).

findings.gap: GAP-228 probe x GAP-229 policy gate
findings.title: Under --dialog accept|dismiss, any popup dialog from a same-renderer opener makes the command fail with a FALSE exit 3: the warden reports the real popup alert (typed) plus a phantom 'unknown' on the opener (collateral getMetrics timeout); the gate accepts the real alert, then 'handles' the phantom -> warden re-probes (now responsive) -> 404 -> DialogBlockedError. stdout still prints dialogPending for the alert that was just accepted, and stderr says 'applying the "accept" policy failed: No dialog is open on that tab'
findings.repro: nav opener; opener runs window.open(url whose script does setTimeout(alert,200)); sutradhar snap --dialog accept (or --dialog dismiss)
findings.rate: 10/10 false exit 3 (accept 5/5, dismiss 5/5); control `dialog accept` 5/5 correct. The opener was not closed in these runs (0/15) because the re-probe came after the real alert had been handled.

findings.title: Performance.getMetrics timing out does NOT mean 'dialog': any renderer main thread blocked outside JavaScript also times it out. A page doing a synchronous XHR is reported as an 'unknown dialog' (snap exits 3), and following the hint (`dialog accept`) CLOSES the healthy tab. Native main-thread work > 400 ms (a large innerHTML parse + layout) makes the warden report 'unknown' for its whole duration. Crashed ('Aw, Snap') and hung (chrome://hang) renderers are also reported as 'unknown dialog' and closed by 'dialog accept'.
findings.repro: page runs setTimeout(()=>{x=new XMLHttpRequest();x.open('GET','/slow?ms=10000',false);x.send()},0); sutradhar snap -> exit 3 unknown; sutradhar dialog accept -> 'Tab <id> was closed ...' and the tab is gone within 0.5-0.8 s
findings.rate: sync XHR: false exit 3 5/5, healthy tab closed by recovery 3/3 (t3 run, closure confirmed by target disappearance 521-769 ms after); 1.96 s native parse+layout: getMetrics timed out 9/9 samples and warden listed the tab as unknown 3/3 while it ran (the snap in this probe landed just after it finished, so 0/3 end-to-end false blocks); ~0.85 s parse+layout: first 400 ms sample blocked 5/5; crashed renderer 2/2 and hung renderer 5/5 reported as 'unknown dialog' and closed by dialog accept. Held (no false block): busy JS 6 s 2/2, forced-layout loop 2/2, allocation/GC-heavy loop 2/2, mid-navigation to a slow response 2/2, background tab with busy timers 2/2, window.print() in headless 2/2, idle 2/2; real alert caught typed 2/2.

findings.title: The ~+130-180 ms per-command cost is NOT the gate. Phase timing shows the gate itself costs 2.6 ms and ensureWarden 1.9 ms; ~100 ms is event-loop linger after the command has finished (raceWithDialog's dialogWatch loop sleeps in a ref'd `await delay(100)` that is never cleared when `stopped` is set, so every process waits out the last 100 ms poll before it can exit), and ~24 ms is extra module load
findings.repro: audit-3/phase-timing-probe.mjs (instrumented temporary copy of dist/cli.js, deleted afterwards, dist sha unchanged)
findings.rate: 12/12 runs: median 'finally end -> process exit' = 99.9 ms; gate 2.6 ms; ensureWarden 1.9 ms; reattach 16.6 ms; module load to main() 223 ms. snap median: branch 390 ms vs master 251 ms (+139) vs pre-FR2-04 loop commit 369cfee 233 ms (a second run, under load: 416 / 260 / 233). Gate-disabled copies of the branch CLI: 378 ms (no gate) and 374 ms (no gate, no ensureWarden) -- i.e. removing the gate saves only ~12-16 ms. Tab scaling (idle tabs): branch 390/392/402/423 ms at 1/5/10/20 tabs vs no-gate 378/376/378/420 -- the warden's /v1/dialogs takes 1-7 ms even at 20 tabs.

findings.title: The recovery message names the tab only by its raw CDP target id ('Tab 95F324D3D9B871FC0A3478711E232758 was closed ...'), not by the CLI tab id that `tabs` prints (tab_sess_...) or its URL, and it is printed with exit 0 by a command the user invoked as `dialog accept`; the preceding dialogPending line (the only place a URL appears) points at the opener, so an agent cannot tell which of its tabs was destroyed. Phantom 'unknown' pending lines for the collaterally blocked opener also trail successful handles (e.g. after `dialog accept` of a popup beforeunload, 3/3).
